results.fact: Whether one 70 m rope reaches every rappel
results.evidence: The route's own description page states a single 70 m rope is required and that parties scramble back to the top of pitch 3 and rappel the route with it. A 2021 first-hand comment on the same page says a 70 m rope does NOT reach when rappelling pitch 3 from the trees directly above the last bolt, though pitches 1-2 rappel fine on a 70. These are the only two accounts found and they disagree; no independent second report exists. A second first-hand report of the pitch-3 rappel (or a measured pitch-3 length) would settle it.

results.correct_value: 2025-26: closed Dec 4, 2025; reopened from the east over Washington Pass April 30, 2026; full highway June 14, 2026
results.evidence: WSDOT's news release (and KOMO) report SR 20 closed for the 2025-26 winter at 6 p.m. Dec 4, 2025 between MP 134 and the Silver Star gate (MP 171), not Dec 12. WSDOT's release and blog (and KIRO) report limited access reopened from the east side up to MP 156.8 at Porcupine Creek (west of Rainy and Washington Passes) on April 30, 2026, with full reopening June 14, 2026. So Washington Pass was drivable from the east from April 30; the stored 'closed Dec 12-June 14' is wrong at both ends for this corridor, while the typical-window fields (roughly early Dec to mid/late April, 'roughly May-November') are rough ranges that agree with that.

results.correct_value: Lexington Tower summit is 7,560 ft; the notch/shoulder where the East Face ends is lower (its height is not published), so 7,621 ft is impossible
results.evidence: Lexington Tower's area page and its encyclopedia entry both give the summit as 7,560 ft (2,304 m); no source gives 7,621 ft. A route overview notes the East Face routes end on a shoulder about 100 ft below the true summit, so the notch pin cannot be 61 ft above it. The notch's own height is unpublished, so the impossible value is cleared rather than replaced; high_point_ft (7,560 = summit) is left as is because the notch height is only approximately known ('about 100 ft below') -- that part stays open. The pin's type 'Summit' is out of scope for this pass.

results.fact: Where a party on 60 m ropes starts rappelling
results.correct_value: On doubled 60 m ropes the first rappel from the top anchor cannot reach the pitch-5 anchor; stop at the fixed nut-and-sling anchor about halfway down pitch 6
results.evidence: The route's description page says the top rappel is from a bolted anchor 20-30 ft above the old pitch-6 slung-block anchor (or partway through the 4th-class scrambling on P7 -- a description of where that TOP anchor sits), that two 70s reach the P5 anchor from it, and that doubled 60s do not, 'in this case you will need to stop at a fixed nut and sling anchor around halfway up P6'. The row's descent_text, rappels, detailed_rack, approach_variants hazards and rappel_detail[0].hazards all agree with that; rappel_count_note and rappel_detail[0].station misread the P7 phrase as a lower starting point for 60 m parties. No second independent source covers the 60 m detail (the other overview only says to rap with two ropes).

results.fact: Parking pass at the pond pullout
results.evidence: The route-page fields say no permit at the informal highway pullout while access.passRequired says Northwest Forest Pass (access.parking_pass itself only lists the Overlook, Blue Lake and Cutthroat trailheads). A regional climbing overview confirms a pass is required at the Washington Pass Overlook and Blue Lake trailheads but says nothing about the pond/hairpin pullout; only one secondary page (not retrievable to verify) says no pass is needed at the hairpin. A Forest Service statement or a second guide on the pond/hairpin pullout would settle it.

results.correct_value: Pitch 2 ends in the notch/nook below the summit ridge; pitch 3 follows the Stegosaur crest to the true summit
results.evidence: A trip report describes pitch 2 ending in a nook below the summit ridge and pitch 3 going up the horned crest called the Stegosaur to the top. A route overview says the North Face goes to the true summit and its last pitch is 4th/low-5th ridge scrambling to the summit. The itinerary's '3 pitches ... to the notch' and 'notch between towers' are the outliers against pitch_detail, waypoints and descent.
